## Open

### T-751 — Move the viewer read API into an orchestrator

> _2026-11-21 · realm/blong-viewer · open_

The viewer realm owns the viewer namespace from its adapter, which is why the plan derives the
realm's Service from the adapter's k8sPorts and the deployment runs --viewer.adapter
and --viewer.gateway and no orchestrator. Give the realm a real orchestrator: move the three
handlers and their handlerGroup from adapter/log to orchestrator, leave the UDP receiver and the
store in the adapter, add orchestrator/viewerDispatch.ts with extends orchestrator.dispatch,
namespace viewer and imports viewer.log, and drop namespace and imports from adapter/log.ts so
exactly one port claims viewer. It is a move and not an addition: the plan renders one flag per
handler group (layerSelectors to deployment.layers to --realm.layer), so a dispatch port with no
group beneath it is activated by nothing and the namespace would lose its claimant. The store stays
a library in the adapter's group and the orchestrator group imports it, because a library is
group-private. Then regenerate the tree and run a deploy cycle: the viewer pod
gains --viewer.orchestrator. This does not touch the ingress path loop, which is about a Service
address and not about which layer answers. Watch the stream: viewer.entry.watch crosses the dispatch
port, so a forwarded iterable has to keep the caller's abort signal if the adapter is ever split
into a process of its own.

## Done

### T-794 — blong-view keeps its cursor and gains the record-carrying option

> _2026-11-24 · realm/blong-viewer · done_

Planned in [#307](https://github.com/feasibleone/blong/issues/307).

`viewer.entry.watch` sends records when the caller asks for them and a cursor otherwise, so the
convention has a second consumer and the old path stays tested. Its page keeps using the cursor (a
log line is not worth a stream frame), but the mode is exercised by a test.

- verify: `blong ./index.ts integration` in `realm/blong-viewer` passes with both modes covered.

Done in realm/blong-viewer. viewer.entry.watch now carries the records by default (entries since the
cursor, plus last and size) and answers {last,size} alone for details:false (D-986); the page passes
details:false because it reads records through viewer.entry.find. The suite was broken before this
change: the integration block never named viewer:{}, so the realm's adapters never attached and
test.viewer.flow resolved to nothing (the run failed with undefined.name inside the chain). With the
block added and both modes asserted, CI=1 blong ./index.ts integration in realm/blong-viewer
exits 0.
